_comment: Grounding regression fixture for bin/fleet_eval_grounding.py.
Every probe here is a question the fleet was actually asked and got wrong, or the
control that proves the retrieval path works at all. Adding a probe is an edit to
this file; the runner carries no query text.
WHY THIS EXISTS. On 2026-08-11 Claudius was asked about the live approval pipeline,
queried the vault correctly, and answered by quoting a decision from 2026-07-09.
Nothing malfunctioned — the vault had never been told about the Buzz migration,
because Praetorium holds no canonical vault credential and box-side work only
reaches the vault when Dave promotes it from the Mac. Retrieval ranks on wording,
not on age, and a superseded document does not announce that it is superseded.
PATH SPELLING. `index` is qmd's spelling (hyphens), `disk` is the on-disk spelling
(underscores). They genuinely differ and retyping one in the other's dialect returns
`No files matched pattern`, which is indistinguishable from the document not
existing. Both are stated so the runner can assert both resolve.
BASELINE. Each probe records the verdict measured when it was added, so the gate
fires on REGRESSION rather than on a state that was already known and accepted.
PASS > POINTER > FAIL. A probe that beats its baseline is reported as an
improvement and the baseline is left alone — bumping it is a deliberate edit, not
something a scheduled job does to its own fixture.
PROBE SHAPE. A probe without `must_answer` asserts a document — did the anchor
rank within `max_rank`, and if not, does the winner's span point at it. A probe
WITH `must_answer` asserts the anchor's own retrieved span: PASS when the span
matches, POINTER when the anchor ranks but its span no longer carries the answer,
FAIL when the anchor drops out of `max_rank` entirely. Both shapes score against
the same PASS > POINTER > FAIL ladder.
ANCHORS ARE LISTS, AND PROBES NAME ONE. Each entry under `anchors` is an ordered
list of candidate documents; the runner resolves it to the first candidate present
in the live index. A fact outlives the document holding it, and the two halves of a
move land from different machines — the vault half is promoted from the Mac, this
file is committed on the box. Naming one file forces both halves into the same
window and mis-scores every run in between: a `must_answer` probe has no pointer
fallback, so it reports a hard FAIL from the moment its fact moves until the fixture
catches up. With a list, either order is safe and the change self-activates.
Every candidate carries its own `pointer`, because the pointer describes the
document that resolved, not the topic.
`routes` moved out of buzz_architecture.md on 2026-08-15 (vault e223a8f). The old
location stays as the second candidate — it is what makes the list worth having,
and removing it is a separate deliberate edit once the split has held for a while.
`architecture` keeps the narrative document, which is what p2/p3 actually assert.
Documents on disk that qmd's walker never picked up. Four vendored skill files
under 08_skills/vp-pitch-deck/vendor/ have sat unindexed since 2026-07-27 — they
are plain files, not symlinks, and every other document in that tree is indexed, so
this is the walker's own rule rather than a stale index. Baselined at 4 so the
count stays quiet and the fifth one — a document no agent could ever retrieve —
shows up. Dot-directories are excluded before counting; qmd indexes none of them.
The load-bearing mechanism. Retrieval is best-effort; this layer is present on
every turn regardless of what `query` ranks first, so its loss is a hard failure
even on a day when all three probes pass.
team_instructions.section: A lookup can also come back full, confident, and a month out of date

_comment: Trend, not gate. The count of documents in the project folder that never mention
the anchor topic — 10 on 2026-08-11. Each one is a document that reads as current
and describes the retired Discord/Hermes/Kanban design. Recorded so the number is
visibly going down instead of being rediscovered.

probes.why: NOT a control, despite being labelled one until 2026-08-15. It was called Buzz-native, and it is not: 'channel', 'scheduled job' and 'report' are Sentinel PRD vocabulary, and three of the four documents it returns are Sentinel briefs. Measured 08-15 on a clean index — the anchor placed 3rd at 0.39 behind prd-08-4c at 0.88, while p4_kind_span's genuinely Buzz-native wording put the same document 1st at 0.93 on the same run. So what this probe measures is whether the route/kind tables outrank a corpus that shares their vocabulary. That is a real question and a harder one than a control, which is why it went red twice from edits with no relation to routes or kinds: 08-11, a six-line insert at the top of the old anchor (rank 1 to rank 3); 08-13, vault commit 5c046b5 rewriting the header blockquote and §6 above the span. index-freshness stayed PASS at 480/480 both times — the index was clean, the chunk boundary was not. Repointed 08-15 at buzz_routes.md, a document whose stated purpose is to sit still.

searches.query: which channel does a scheduled job publish its report to, and what event kind does it need?

probes.why: The plainly-worded version of the same question. On 2026-08-11 this returned agent-inbox-sync/SKILL.md first and the anchor fourth at 0.44; after two supersession banners were added it returned inbox_workflow.md first, which mentions Buzz nowhere at all. Bannering two documents promoted an unbannered third. Stays on the architecture anchor: this asks how the workforce publishes and approves, which is narrative, not the route table. This is the least stable probe in the fixture — across 13 recorded runs its anchor has been absent (08-11, 08-12), rank 1 (08-13 to 08-15, seven runs) and absent again (08-16) without the vault's answer to the question changing once, because the field is near-tied: ranks 2 through 8 span 0.53 down to 0.39, so chunk movement anywhere in the folder reorders it. Neither transition was an edit about publishing or approval. The gain is not isolable to one commit — five publishes in that window touched nine documents in this folder, including inbox_workflow.md, the incumbent winner. The loss is vault 13d3a94 (08-15 13:04) rewriting the write-boundary bullet in section 6 and expanding agent_branch_workflow.md by 38 lines, which moved the anchor's retrieved span to `@@ -51,4 @@` and its rank to 6 at 0.41, behind vision.md at 0.90. BASELINE HISTORY: bumped FAIL to PASS on 2026-08-15, reverted to FAIL on 2026-08-16, restored to PASS on 2026-08-17. Recorded rather than quietly rewritten, because every leg is informative. The 08-15 bump had seven runs over four days behind it and still did not survive a fifth, so run count is not evidence of stability for a probe scoring inside a 0.14-wide band; it also carried a wrong cause, crediting the buzz_routes split, which landed 08-15, two days after the gain. The 08-16 reversion was the right call on the evidence available then. The 08-17 restore rests on a controlled experiment rather than a run count: two full-vault scratch indexes, 497 documents each, differing in exactly the section 6 line — control anchor absent (FAIL) against treatment anchor rank 1 (PASS), with ranks 3 through 8 identical between the two runs. That isolates the cause to one line and makes PASS an achievable state, so the baseline is a target again rather than a record of breakage. The restore deliberately lands BEFORE the fix does: the vault edit is on branch agents/2026-08-16-buzz-arch-s6-source-of-truth (commit 2c4ffe2), awaiting a Mac merge and a boxsafe publish, so this probe reads REGRESSION until both happen. That is the intent — a baseline lowered to match a break reports green while the vault stays wrong. CAUTION when reading the scores quoted above: the ladder 0.92 / 0.53 / 0.46 / 0.44 / 0.41 recurs run after run regardless of which document occupies each slot, so score here is close to positional and only rank is evidence — the 0.41 and 0.90 figures name slots, not quality. RESOLVED, was OPEN (2026-08-17): repointing the anchor is not the remedy. Measured with this runner against the live field, a true repoint to agent_branch_workflow lifts the anchor only to rank 3, still failing max_rank 2 — and appending it as a second candidate is a no-op, because resolve_anchors is first-present-wins, so while buzz_architecture.md is indexed it always wins the resolution. The section 6 duplication was the fault, not the anchor choice: it restated evidence that agent_branch_workflow section 5 and open_loops #17 already owned, and that re-cut every chunk below it.

searches.query: how does the agent workforce publish its work and get proposals approved today?

probes.why: Claudius's exact failure. The top hit carried a supersession banner at lines 6-10 and the retrieved span was line 85 — the pointer existed and was outside the window the agent saw. This probe is the reason the span, not the document, is what gets checked. Narrative question, so it keeps the architecture anchor.

searches.query: are we still building the NUC implementation cards, and what was decided about the approval gate?
NUC-25b approval gate decision Notion inbox status

probes.why: The placement guard. The other three probes assert which document wins; this one asserts that the anchor's own retrieved span still contains the answer, because those are different failures. A document is represented in results by ONE chunk, so prose added anywhere above re-cuts every boundary below it and the chunk that used to answer stops existing while the file keeps ranking first. Measured 2026-08-11: a six-line section inserted at the top of the anchor knocked p1_route_kind from rank 1 to rank 3, and only luck made that visible — a smaller shift would have kept rank 1 and quietly handed the agent a window with no answer in it. The answer chosen is the forum root-post kind, `45001`, because it is a single token that is either in the window or is not, and because sending kind 9 into a forum is the exact mistake this vault section exists to prevent (buzz_architecture §3). Measured PASS on the live index: anchor rank 1, span `@@ -44,4 @@`, deterministic over three runs. Repointed 2026-08-15 at buzz_routes.md, which now carries the kind table; this is the probe that made the anchor a list, because a `must_answer` probe has no pointer fallback and would have hard-FAILED for every run between the vault promotion and this edit.
